regions.name: flow_near_wake
regions.why: This is the exact flow_requirement:near_wake volume and it currently has configured_volume_coverage 0.0, which is the sole reason scenario_screen is rejected. Level 3 gives h = 0.1305/2^3 = 0.0163 m = 0.39x the required max_cell_axis_span 0.04225 m (= H/8), so the recirculating bubble, base shear layers and C-pillar vortices get ~2.6x more cells across the shear layer than level 2 would allow and the box retains margin against the native 1.5x p95 tolerance. Level 3 equals the global surface level, so no hanging-node cliff is created where the wake box meets the body surface, and the box is inside the domain (domain extends to x ~ 5.12, y +/-1.14, z from about -0.51 upward).

regions.name: flow_far_wake
regions.why: Exact flow_requirement:far_wake volume, also at configured_volume_coverage 0.0. The region contains 0 geometry samples and finite_fluid_gap_fraction 0.0, so it is pure off-body fluid that only transports the velocity deficit and residual shear. Level 2 gives h = 0.0326 m = 0.39x the required 0.0845 m (= H/4); level 1 (0.0653 m) would pass the nominal limit but with only 1.29x margin and coarser box-boundary cells, while the extra cost of level 2 is small (~26k cells) relative to the 2,000,000 budget, so level 2 is the better cost/robustness trade for a downstream transport zone.

regions.name: flow_base_shear
regions.why: Targets the shear-layer/C-pillar-vortex generation region at the slant and base periphery, which is the source term of flow_requirement:near_wake ('rear separation, shear layers and recirculating vehicle wake'). The existing physical_refinement_bands stop at 0.0979 m from the wall (level 2 = 0.0326 m) while the wake box is 0.0163 m; starting refinement only at x = 0.944 would place a cell-size step of 2x across the separation origin, degrading shear-layer thickness and vortex-core resolution exactly where they are set. The box uses the same transverse/vertical bounds as the near-wake box so the two refined volumes are contiguous over x = 0.62-1.988 with no internal step; solid cells inside the body footprint are discarded by snappy, so the real added volume is only the ~0.05-0.08 m3 of fluid above, beside and below the base (about 19k cells). Level 3 is within +2 of the global surface level 3.

best_provisional_candidate.grade: provisional: still requires complete layers and sane flow; no industrial accuracy certificate

advisor.hypothesis: Round 1 (plan:974f4a19a933d69d) failed for two independent reasons, neither of which is the wake-box layout: (1) a local snap/layer catastrophe at the right rear C-pillar corner near (0.61, 0.10, 0.045) — postProcessing/constant/nonOrthoFaces:4 (max_non_ortho 147.4 vs limit 70), wrongOrientedFaces:15 (the 3 failing checkMesh non-ortho errors) and lowQualityTetFaces:13 all coincide within a box of ~0.07 m at 4.2-5.3 mm wall distance, where discrete_normal_rotation_per_metre p95 is ~100 rad/m; (2) layer extrusion suppressed at the remaining wall: only 26 351 of 26 393 body faces extruded and the split areas (0.0016, 0.0719, 0.0747 ... of body area) show ~26% of the wall losing 1-4 layers, so coverage is 0.735 not 0.9. The medial mover reduced thickness at 2988 nodes for thickness-to-medial ratio, meaning the requested stack (14.4 mm) exceeds available fluid medial distance around the body. I therefore restore the measured-valid anchor plan:4d3de347a962a86f (native checkMesh 0 failures, max_non_ortho 64.9<65, fidelity accepted, 275 605 cells) and apply a conservative, non-splitting layer/tolerance change plus targeted resolution only where the corner defect lives. Crucially the anchor already contains all six flow boxes; round-1 relative to that anchor only ADDED repair_0 (level 4 over the whole vehicle) and REMOVED one layer (8->7). Thus restoring the anchor and NOT re-adding repair_0 reproduces the anchor's 64.9-degree non-ortho field while keeping configured coverage of both flow_requirement volumes, which the anchor already satisfied. The layer repair is chosen so that wall coverage improves without recreating the corner geometry offence.
advisor.expected_change: 1) Native checkMesh returns to the anchor's 0 failures and max_non_ortho <= 65 (reference 64.93) because the level-4 repair_0 box that created the 147.4-degree corner faces is not re-added. 2) body area with >=5 layers rises from anchor 0.492 / round-1 0.735 toward >=0.90 by reducing n_surface_layers 8->6 (stack 8.26 mm '=' 0.5x the existing 16.3 mm band cell) which cuts the count of medial-distance thickness reductions below 2988 (2988 of ~26.4k wall nodes, i.e. 11% of the wall); feature_angle 60->80 removes the suppression mechanism flagged by fraction_adjacent_edges_above_layer_feature_angle = 0.0158; the exp(-0.5^2)=0.78 wall-distance proxy shows 8.26 mm reaches far more target points than 14.4 mm; ~53 of the 119-171 shortfall:2/3 faces at z>=0.30 lie within 8.3 mm wall distance of the upper rear corner. 3) Level 4 on the corner box lowers the defect-region cell width from 16.3 mm to 8.16 mm (0.5x the 0.389 m measured local feature), so explicit feature snapping of the C-pillar edge is resolved by ~2 cells instead of ~1. 4) Peak u_tau moves at most ~2.9% (Cf ~ Re^-1/5 for 8->6 layers), so actual y+ p50 stays ~48-50 at 30 m/s and the frozen target_yplus=50 is still met; first_layer_thickness is untouched. Uncertainty: the shrinkage does not fix boundary layer corner interactions at the base periphery; the added cells (~3.5e5) are unvalidated and the 1.5x p95 mandate remains satisfied only if native bins confirm the level-4 box reaches the base.
counterevidence: The measured-valid anchor plan:4d3de347a962a86f yields only 0.492 layer coverage with native checkMesh 0 failures; layer coverage and quality are anti-correlated across the two measured rounds, so a quality-safe layer change may still miss the 0.90 gate.

round0 and round1 both used first_layer_thickness 0.0011138897093318702 (y+ p50 50.0) and both stack top layers at 0.0621/0.6093 of wall area: layer count truncation is measureable in the existing data, but no measured flow field exists, so the y+ consequence of 8->6 layers is inferred from Cf scaling, not measured wall shear.

layer_shortfall:0 has fluid_gap p50 0.4454 m (not a thin-gap cluster); its deficits come from thickness-to-medial truncation, and no medial-distance samples exist inside that box, so I cannot quantify how many of the 884 points the shorter stack will recover.
native_thickness_truncation is an unweighted, possibly processor-duplicated subset (1500 of 2988 lines in the measured box), so it bounds, not measures, the truncation fraction.

The level-4 corner box bounds apex x=0.6621 slightly beyond the body trailing x=0.944? No: 0.6621 < 0.944 and the body top is z=0.338, so the box is a solid overlap region whose interior bins are discarded by snappy — the (0.55,0.20,0.0) bin is exactly the bin containing the round-1 wrongOrientedFaces centroid (0.612, 0.103, 0.046).
The anchor's patch counts (minY 1653) differ from round1 (minX 870), so streamwise cell size rose between rounds; that change is separate from the layer degradation and is not claimed as a cause.
alternatives: Restore anchor and change only layer_settings (6 layers, feature_angle 80): quality-safe but leaves the >70 non-ortho failures unaddressed, so acceptance fails on quality regardless of layer coverage.
Restore anchor and add only the level-4 corner box, no layer change: keeps anchor coverage 0.492, far under the 0.90 gate.

Restore anchor with wall_height scale 0.5 (0.00056 m first cell): reduces stack height to ~7.2 mm, but doubles y+ to ~100, forfeiting the immutable y+~50 plan without any measured wall shear — rejected.

Restore round1 (plan:974f4a19a933d69d) and patch the corner with snap_settings only: inadmissible because that anchor is not eligible_for_restore (it already contains the 147-degree faces), and snap-only smoothing cannot reorient 6 incorrectly-oriented face pyramids.

actions.why: plan:4d3de347a962a86f is the only eligible anchor with native checkMesh 0 failures and max_non_ortho 64.93 < 65, fidelity accepted, 275605 cells; it already contains flow_near_wake (level 3), flow_far_wake (level 2) and flow_base_shear (level 3), i.e. the measured native near_wake p95 0.0225 m and far_wake p95 0.0330 m that PASSED both flow_requirement mandates. Restoring it removes round-1's whole-vehicle level-4 repair_0 region, which is the direct cause of the 147.4-degree non-ortho faces and the 3 failing checkMesh checks. Layer baseline is taken from the ANCHOR, not the failed round-1 spec: n_surface_layers 8, first_layer_thickness 0.0011138897 m, expansion_ratio 1.2, feature_angle 60, mesh_shrinker displacementMedialAxis.

Boundary-layer SHORTFALL repair, not a growth pass. Round-1 evidence shows only 26351/26393 body faces extruded and 2988 nodes where native medialAxisMeshMover truncated layer thickness for thickness-to-medial ratio, so the requested 14.39 mm stack exceeds available FLUID medial distance around the body; 26% of wall area therefore carries 1-4 layers. Lowering n_surface_layers to 6 shrinks the stack to 8.26 mm, exactly 0.5x the existing 16.3125 mm global surface band cell (16.3125*0.1=1.63<167.4 and 1.63125e-1<167.4), which removes the requested-outer-layer 3.33 mm > half the first band cell 16.3/2=8.16 mm mismatch that drives a 2:1 jump onto the last layer; an exp(-0.5^2)=0.78 proxy of wall points needing <=8.26 mm versus 14.39 mm bounds the recoverable area. Raising feature_angle 60->80 removes the layer-suppression mechanism measured as fraction_adjacent_edges_above_layer_feature_angle = 0.0158 in layer_shortfall:0 (884 faces) and 0.0181 in layer_shortfall:2 (171 faces), without touching the snap-time resolve_feature_angle 30 or the body patch. max_thickness_to_medial_ratio 0.3->0.45 lets the medial mover keep thickness where fluid medial distance is 18.4-27.5 mm, the regime reported by native_thickness_truncation p50 0.0176 m / p95 0.0341 m. n_smooth_thickness 10->16 and n_layer_iter 50->60 give more native shrinkage passes. If native area_fraction favours the short layers (0.0021,0.0844,0.0843,0.0849,0.0848,0.0791,0.0760,0.5053), n_outer_iter 1->2 re-partitions the stack outer-to-inner to spread truncation instead of killing the top layer; the installed v2412 driver supports this. first_layer_thickness is deliberately UNCHANGED: 0.0011138897 m reproduced y+ p50 = 50.0 in round0 AND round1 at 30 m/s, so it stays inside the 0.5-2x band and no measured wall shear is required to justify it.

Repairs the single measured cat sastrophe that produced the failure messages. postProcessing/constant/nonOrthoFaces:4 (3 faces, max_non_ortho 147.4), postProcessing/constant/wrongOrientedFaces:15 (3 faces) and lowQualityTetFaces:13 / meshQualityFaces:14 (10 faces each) all sit in the SAME 0.07 m cluster at centroid ~(0.6116, 0.1011, 0.0448), 4.2-5.3 mm off the wall, where discrete_normal_rotation_per_metre p95 = 100 rad/m — a high-curvature C-pillar/upper-rear corner where explicit feature snapping of a level-3 (16.3 mm) surface has no cell interior to snap to. Level 4 halves the local surface cell to 8.16 mm, which is 0.5x the measured local full feature 0.389 m scale (=0.1945 m half-thickness), so resolution rather than cell deformation absorbs the corner. Level 4 is exactly +1 of the global surface level 3, below the +2 limit. The box covers x 0.47-0.67 (crossing the slant/base junction), the full y extent of the measured cluster (-0.10..0.21) and z up to 0.11 just above the body top 0.338? No: z max 0.11 is below 0.338, so it is an interior body-footprint volume whose fluid bins are the beside/slat regions -- hence the y range must extend to both sides to be useful; note most of this box is solid/inside the shell and is discarded, keeping cost bounded.

Complementary transition/tolerance repair instead of more boxes. Round-1 round left 3 non-ortho errors and 6 wrongly-oriented face pyramids at a 4-5 mm welded-corner wall distance while the implicit path was DISABLED (implicit_feature_snap false). Enabling implicit_feature_snap moves resolution of the high-curvature C-pillar edge from an explicit displacement of level-3 cells into the implicit feature solve, which is the mechanism that produced the 100 rad/m normal rotation; tolerance 2.0->1.5 aligns the snap region with the 8.16 mm level-4 cells (<=1.5*8.16 mm) and n_feature_snap_iter 10->24 gives the feature snap more passes to relax the 6 bad pyramids without moving the wall surface (fidelity: bidirectional p99 1.95e-4 m, area/volume errors 1.6e-4, so the surface itself is fine — the defect is the first cell layer, not the geometry).
